subject: gnomeTinkerer
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: gnome tinkerer with a backpack of gadgets.
Style: whimsical low-poly mix.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I'm noticing the hat's steam puffs appear to float beside it rather than connecting naturally, and the bulb at the tip is mostly hidden from the front view, only showing clearly from the side.

The face could use attention too — the brim sits a bit low over the forehead, partially cutting into eye level, so I'm considering enlarging the eyes slightly and nudging the hat up a touch. The arms look stiff in the A-pose with thin, undersized hands that could use more "chunky" scaling, and the torso seems a bit thin relative to the bulky backpack.

Checking the rest of the gear: the hammer and wrench placements on the hips look fine, as does the lantern rod and bedroll end cap peeking out the back. In side view though, the steam puffs cluster messily near the hat tip and spring antenna, so I want to shift the pipe and puffs further to the side to clean that up.

The goggles, beard, and moustache all look good, and the gnome fills the base nicely at the center. I'm now considering whether the underside of the drooping hat tip needs more attention in the lighting.

Looking at the three-quarter face, the cheeks and ears read fine, and the pants' patch pattern is acceptable even if a bit scale-like. The bigger issue is that the beard covers almost the entire apron decal, hiding its pocket details -- but since the beard is such a signature feature, I'll keep it as is rather than shortening it, even though this leaves most of the apron hidden below the belt area.

The shoulder strap and pack roll both read fine despite partial occlusion by the hat. For the hands, I want to scale up the palm and finger radii and lengthen the fingers slightly to make them read better at small sizes. I'm also planning to enlarge the eye decals and nudge their azimuth outward to avoid overlapping with the brow and brim as they grow.

Checking the eye vertical placement against the brim edge and brow line, I decide to lower the elevation slightly so the eye top stays clear of the brim. Boots sit correctly on the ground plane, and the ankle cuff reads fine as a fold-down detail. Looking at the whole figure, the main weak points are the stubby, stiff legs and the tiny hands — the hat and face proportions seem fine, and the beard/moustache cover the mouth area adequately.

The torso reads narrow but the shirt arms look okay in 3/4 view. The toolbox sign text is legible and only slightly overlaps the hammer, which is acceptable, and the sparse grass tufts are fine too. I'm planning a few fixes: enlarge the eyes and hands, consider pupil glints, and maybe add a small glowing accent like a lamp or crystal spark somewhere on the figure for visual interest, while keeping the hidden bulb and gauge face as they are. I also notice some grey tuft shapes near the eye corners under the hat that read as sideburn hair.

Now I'm drafting the precise search-and-replace edits: adjusting the eye decal's position and size parameters, widening the palm capsule radius, and lengthening the finger definitions with adjusted radii and offsets to keep them from overlapping awkwardly given the larger palm size.
